result: Ventricular CSF lactate by 1H MRSI, normed across two studies, was higher in CFS, FM and CFS+FM than healthy controls, with no difference among the three patient groups.
reason: Same measure and direction, but data pooled from the same group's earlier cohorts, so not independent; adds FM comparison showing lactate is not CFS-specific

result: Giardia-specific CD4 T-cell activation, proliferation and cytokines did not differ between post-Giardia CFS (n=15) and other exposed groups; sCD40L was raised in fatigued groups and correlated with fatigue.
reason: Finding is about post-outbreak fatigue incidence; paper measures antigen-specific immune responses, which no atlas finding covers

result: In ALSPAC, chronic disabling fatigue prevalence rose from 1.47% at 13 to 2.99% at 18; about 75% with CDF at one age no longer met it 2-3 years later, and 8% persisted through adolescence.
reason: Adds adolescent course (better prognosis than adults), though CDF is a questionnaire proxy, not clinical diagnosis

result: In 15 CFS/ME vs 25 controls, unstimulated CD56bright NK cells had fewer TRPM3 receptors, but baseline Ca2+ flux did not differ and PregS-stimulated CD56bright cells showed increased, not reduced, Ca2+ flux.
reason: Same group; TRPM3 expression lower but the calcium influx measure was unchanged or raised, against the finding's reduced-influx claim

result: Plasma RNA metagenomics in 25 ME/CFS vs Lyme, SLE and 25 healthy controls found very little microbial RNA, and the few group differences were explained by contamination and batch effects.
reason: Independent unbiased blood sequencing study finding no excess microbes in ME/CFS

result: On active stand, POTS was present in 5.7% of 419 adults with CFS vs 6.9% of non-CFS fatigued adults (P=0.54), and 18.2% vs 17.4% in adolescents; POTS was unrelated to severity or activity.
reason: Supports minority/variable prevalence (low end, higher in adolescents) rather than contradicting it; adds fatigued comparison group showing no excess

result: Meta-analysis of 7 studies (159 patients, 47 effects): a single exercise bout increased fatigue more in ME/CFS than controls (delta 0.73, 95% CI 0.24-1.23), with larger increases measured 4 h or more after exercise.
reason: Pooled controlled evidence supporting delayed worsening; a meta-analysis rather than an independent cohort with the same measure

result: In a Norwegian national registry of 1,670 children with CFS/ME, infectious mononucleosis was recorded in the prior 2 years for 11.1% vs 0.5% of children with type 1 diabetes, with infections, depression, anxiety, migraine and muscle pain also more common.
reason: Retrospective registry enrichment of prior infection, not prospective post-mono CFS rates; fits the registry prior-viral-infection finding
